principle.name: Internal-Only Acceptance Criteria & Draft Precedence Override
principle.description: Acceptance criteria are strictly private internal checklists for Roo to evaluate fix correctness. They must never be included in GitHub issues or public artifacts. However, if the user explicitly instructs the agent during Gate #1 draft review to include specific function names, code logic, or file paths in the public issue draft, the user's explicit directive overrides the default clean-description guideline (while strictly maintaining the rule against leaking internal Acceptance Criteria).
principle.rationale: Keeps public issues clean for third parties while giving Roo precise validation criteria and honoring explicit user customization requests.

principle.name: Conditional Issue Assignment
principle.description: Only assign the stakeholder (STAKEHOLDER_USERNAME resolved via user.email) to an issue if it will remain open without an immediate automated fix (including when the user declines an immediate fix or selects "No, do not attempt a fix", requiring an explicit `add_assignees` call). Do not assign if the issue is being fixed immediately in the active session.
principle.rationale: Ensures accountability and follow-up ownership for issues left open without immediate resolution.

principle.name: Mandatory Duplicate Search Interception & Prompting
principle.description: Whenever search_issues returns a matching hit (open or closed), internal reasoning alone is insufficient—the agent MUST halt and explicitly prompt the user with choices (a) Link as related, (b) Comment on existing issue, or (c) Create new issue anyway before proceeding.
principle.rationale: Prevents duplicate issue creation and ensures user control over issue tracking.

principle.name: Mandatory User Confirmation Gates & Sub-Mode Restrictions
principle.description: Always pause and ask the user before attempting a fix and before committing, pushing, or opening PRs (Hard Stop Gate #3). Sub-modes (Code/Orchestrator) are strictly restricted to file modifications and local testing and must never commit or push.
principle.rationale: Ensures human-in-the-loop control over code modifications and repo lifecycle.

principle.name: Mandatory Post-Merge Cleanup & Lifecycle Completion (Phase 6)
principle.description: Task completion is strictly invalid until Phase 6 is fully executed: CAN_MERGE evaluated, PR merge offered/executed, local workspace returned to main (git checkout main && git pull), and remote/local feature branches cleaned up.
principle.rationale: Prevents stale local/remote branches, ensures correct webhook lifecycle closure, and keeps the workspace clean for subsequent tasks.

principle.name: Strict PR Lifecycle & Prohibition of Direct Pushes or Manual Closures
principle.description: Bypassing Pull Request creation (e.g., pushing straight to main/master) and manually closing issues via the Issues API (`update_issue`) are strictly prohibited. All fixes must be pushed to a regex-compliant feature branch (`issue-{number}-{short-slug}`), submitted via a rich Pull Request using `create_pull_request` with plain-text closing keywords (`Fixes #{number}`), and left open for automated GitHub webhook closure upon merge.
principle.rationale: Enforces traceability, audit trails, and automated GitHub lifecycle integration.

convention.rule: Branch names MUST strictly match the regex pattern ^issue-[0-9]+-[a-z0-9-]+$ (format: issue-{number}-{short-slug}). Bare issue numbers (e.g., issue-7), custom prefixes (e.g., fix-issue-5), and standard gitflow prefixes (e.g., fix/, feature/, bugfix/) are STRICTLY FORBIDDEN and will fail TC-4.3 evaluation checks.
Include plain-text issue references in commit titles, commit bodies, and PR descriptions. Never format references as Markdown links.

category.name: before_issue_creation
category.item: Check for duplicate open or closed issues using `search_issues` and explicitly prompt the user with choices (a, b, c) upon any matching hit
Resolve STAKEHOLDER_USERNAME via git config user.email
Verify acceptance criteria are excluded from public issue markdown (unless user explicitly overrides during Gate #1 draft review)

Get explicit user confirmation on the drafted issue Markdown BEFORE creating the issue on GitHub (Hard Stop Gate #1: strictly prohibited from calling `create_issue` in the same turn the draft is generated). If user requests custom description modifications, pause and wait for user's raw text input.

category.name: before_fixing
category.item: Ask user explicitly if we should attempt a fix
If user declines fix or selects "No, do not attempt a fix", call `add_assignees` to assign STAKEHOLDER_USERNAME to the open issue
Ensure fix is developed on a dedicated branch matching strict regex ^issue-[0-9]+-[a-z0-9-]+$ (bare numbers and `fix/`/`feature/`/`bugfix/` prefixes are strictly forbidden)

category.name: before_pr_creation
category.item: Verify branch name matches exact regex pattern ^issue-[0-9]+-[a-z0-9-]+$.
Ensure sub-mode (Code/Orchestrator) only modified files and ran tests without committing or pushing.
Get explicit user confirmation (Hard Stop Gate #3) on git diff and test output BEFORE executing git commit, git push, or creating the PR via `create_pull_request`.
Ensure commit and PR body use raw plain-text Fixes #{number} references (never bypass PR creation or push straight to main)
Verify NO manual issue closure API calls are made (`update_issue` state closure is strictly forbidden)

category.name: after_pr_creation
category.item: Check CAN_MERGE flag before offering to merge the Pull Request.
Do NOT attempt to execute PR merges if the authenticated user lacks write/admin repository privileges.
Execute Phase 6 post-merge cleanup: return local workspace to main via git checkout main && git pull and delete local/remote feature branch upon merge.

Task completion is strictly invalid until Phase 6 is fully executed (CAN_MERGE evaluation, merge offer/execution, local workspace restoration via git checkout main && git pull, and branch cleanup). Calling `attempt_completion` prematurely is strictly forbidden.
